key_insight: You can validly compare LLM safety without labeled benchmarks by treating scenario-based audits as evidence under a precise contract: scores are meaningful only relative to a fixed scenario pack, rubric, auditor, judge, sampling plan, and rerun budget. The paper formalizes this benchmarkless comparative safety scoring and practical validation constraints.
problem_solved: How to evaluate and compare candidate language models for safety when no ground-truth labeled benchmark exists for the target language, sector, or regulatory regime.
method: Formalize the benchmarkless comparative safety setting and define a validity contract that fixes: scenario pack, rubric, auditor, judge, sampling configuration, and rerun budget.

Replace reliance on unavailable ground-truth labels by using scenario-based audits plus repeatability/consistency checks and controlled sampling to produce comparable safety scores with well-specified scope.
Provide a validation/interpretation framework that quantifies when comparative scores can be treated as deployment evidence and clarifies their limitations.
impact: Gives practitioners a rigorous, operational way to compare model safety where labeled data don’t exist, reducing deployment risk by making evaluation assumptions explicit and results reproducible. It also sets clear boundaries for what such scores can (and cannot) imply.
visual_elements: Contract diagram showing the six fixed components (scenario pack, rubric, auditor, judge, sampling, rerun budget) as inputs that determine score validity
Flowchart of scenario-based audit: sample → prompt scenarios → collect outputs → judge/rubric → score → rerun/repeatability loop
Bar chart or dot-and-interval plot comparing models with uncertainty bars and annotation of the fixed-scope constraint
Checklist/icon set summarizing dos and don’ts for interpreting scores (e.g., ‘Valid only if same contract’, ‘Not a universal ground truth’)
paper_title: When No Benchmark Exists: Validating Comparative LLM Safety Scoring Without Ground-Truth Labels
paper_authors: Sushant Gautam, Finn Schwall, Annika Willoch Olstad, Fernando Vallecillos Ruiz, Birk Torpmann-Hagen
